title: Find the hidden constant from one known output
subtitle: Linear functions · 13 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **13 of the official questions in Linear functions are this one** — 2 Easy, 8 Medium, 3 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The function has a letter constant (a slope or intercept named with a letter) and you're given one input-output pair in f(number) = number form.
- You're asked for the constant, or for a different output once the constant is known.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Substitute the known input and output into the rule.
- 2) Solve the resulting one-variable equation for the constant.
- 3) If the question asks for a new output, rewrite the function with the constant filled in and evaluate at the new input.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Enter the rule with the constant as a slider, or enter the equation you get after substituting and let Desmos solve for the constant.
This helps when the numbers are messy.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You stop after finding the constant when the question asked for a second output.
Or you mix up the input and output when substituting.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
